title: Napoleon wasn't short. Britain made you think so.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: You think Napoleon was tiny. He was about average.
beats.visual: David's 'Napoleon in His Study' with a height ruler sliding up beside him

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In France, his doctor and valet recorded Napoleon at five foot two.
beats.visual: Sketch measuring rod marked '5 pieds 2 pouces'

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Not exactly. French inches were longer. But there was a problem: Britain was at war with him.
beats.visual: Two rulers side by side, the French inch visibly longer; British and French flags clash

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: About 1.67 metres, roughly five foot six: average for his time.
beats.visual: Silhouette lineup: average Frenchman, Napoleon, tall Old Guard grenadier in bearskin

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Then where did tiny come from?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Cartoons. From 1803, Britain's James Gillray drew him as Little Boney, a toddler throwing tantrums.
beats.visual: PD Gillray 'Maniac Ravings, or Little Boney in a Strong Fit' (1803), zoom on the tantrum

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The joke outlived him: today we say Napoleon complex.
beats.visual: Text card 'Napoleon complex' with a crossed-out ruler

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Napoleon wasn't short. Britain made you think so. Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
beats.visual: Lefevre portrait returns, ruler at average; History Sketches corner logo

description: Napoleon was recorded at 5 foot 2 in French units, about 1.67 m or 5 foot 6 today, roughly average for his time. British cartoonist James Gillray turned him into 'Little Boney'. Narration: synthetic voices. Facts checked against two sources. #history #shorts #napoleon #mythbusting
